# All translations of the admitted quartic family are excluded as separators

25 October 2026. This is a completed, bounded discriminator for the ACTUAL contracted laws. It is not a full Morrey resolution or proof that those laws are laminates.

## Certified result

For every real 2-by-2 background A and every a in [-1,1], define

    W_a(X)=|X|_F^4+4a |X|_F^2 det X+(6a^2-2)(det X)^2.

For the actual full first root nu_1 of the correlated cosine law,

    integral W_a(A+B(z)) dnu_1(z)-W_a(A) > 1.

The SAME strict bound holds for the actual first randomized-and-ball-peeled law

    eta=omega delta_0+[f(z)-m0 1_(B_R)(z)] dz,
    R=sqrt(3)/2, m0=1/(10pi^2), omega=sqrt(3)/(20pi).

Its normalized continuous residual has gap greater than 1/(1-omega), hence also greater than 1. The statements include nonsymmetric backgrounds and parameter-endpoint sequences whose optimizing backgrounds diverge to infinity.

Thus no member of this entire translated, untransformed quartic family rejects either specified contraction branch. Arbitrary physical left/right anisotropic transforms are NOT covered. Nor is the later freshly renewed-and-repeeled descendant silently substituted for eta.

## 1. Global admission is independently proved

    (1/2) D^2 W_a(X)[E11,E11]
      =6(x+a y)^2+2(b-a c)^2+2(1-a^2)c^2>=0.

Every rank-one direction can be brought to a multiple of E11 by left/right SO(2) rotations, which preserve |X|_F and det X. This proves global admission, including all translations, without relying on sampled Hessians or on the separate quasiconvexity theorem cited by the recovered source.

## 2. Only ten source moments are needed

# Exact all-background reduction for the admitted planar quartics

25 October 2026. This is an algebraic reduction, not a sampled search. It applies to the actual first conditional-root law and, through the explicit inequality below, the actual randomized-and-ball-peeled law. Numerical moment certification is a separate obligation.

## 1. Coordinates and exact gap

Write every real 2 by 2 background, including nonsymmetric ones, uniquely as

A = [[t+p,h+r],[h-r,t-p]].

For the symmetric random increment X=B(u,v,w), put

τ=(u+v+2w)/2, y=((u-v)/2,w).

Let m=Eτ²=E|y|², c=E(τy), M=E(yyᵀ), and let

m1=Eτ³, m2=E(τ|y|²), m3=E(τ²y), m4=E(|y|²y).

The equality defining m is exactly E det X=0. Mean zero is also required. Set

α=2(a+1)(3a+1), β=12(1-a²), γ=2(a-1)(3a-1).

Then W_a=α(t²+r²)²+β(t²+r²)(p²+h²)+γ(p²+h²)². Its translated expectation gap is exactly

G_a(A)=k(a)+zᵀQ(a)z+ℓ(a)ᵀz+16m(a+1)r²,

where z=(t,p,h), k(a)=E W_a(X),

Qtt=24m(a+1)²,
Qt,y=24(1-a)(1+a)cᵀ,
Qy,y=8(1-a)[2m I-(3a-1)M],

ℓt=8(a+1)L,
ℓy=8(1-a)N,
L=(3a+1)m1+3(1-a)m2,
N=3(1+a)m3-(3a-1)m4.

All terms here follow by polynomial expansion; no convexity premise was used. The formula remains valid for a signed moment functional of total mass one, mean zero and determinant moment zero.

The skew coordinate has no linear or mixed term. For -1<a≤1 its unique minimizing value is r=0, provided m>0. At a=-1 it is flat. In particular, optimizing only symmetric backgrounds is justified only after this calculation, not as an assumption.

## 2. Stable elimination and parameter endpoints

For -1<a<1 set x=(1+a)t. Completing the square in x and then in b=(p,h) gives

D(a)=2m I-(3a-1)M-3(1-a)ccᵀ/m,
v(a)=N-Lc/m,

F(a)=inf_A G_a(A)
    =k(a)-(2/3)L²/m-2(1-a)vᵀD(a)^{-1}v,

provided D(a) is positive definite. The minimizing background is

b*=-(1/2)D(a)^{-1}v,
x*= -L/(6m)-(1-a)cᵀb*/m,
t*=x*/(1+a), r*=0.

The correct unrestricted quadratic criterion is Q positive semidefinite and ℓ in its range; otherwise the infimum is minus infinity. When it holds, the value is k-ℓᵀQ^+ℓ/4, and all optimizers are -Q^+ℓ/2+ker Q. The present D bounds below give the stronger positive-definite condition for every interior parameter.

At a=1 the exact endpoint is W_1=16(t²+r²)². The p,h directions are flat, and

inf_A G_1(A)=k(1)-(32/3)m1²/m,
t*=-m1/(3m), r*=0.

# Certified moments of the actual contracted cosine law

This is a bounded, deterministic interval proof for the actual law ν₁ = R#ν, where ν is the Haar cosine law. It computes no randomized-peel moments, no optimization, and no trajectory.

## Formula and scope

Let x,y be independent uniform phases in [0,2π]. Set u=cos x, v=cos y, w=cos(x+y), B=−9+8u−4v−4w, C=2u+4u(v+w)−2vw−4(v+w), D=B²+32C, and m=2C/(3√D−B). Then (U,V,W)=(u−m,v+2m,w+2m). The moments use τ=(U+V+2W)/2, y₁=(U−V)/2, y₂=W, and H=y₁²+y₂².

The covariance identity Cov(ν₁)=I/2−sddᵀ, d=(−1,2,2), is a separate exact structural identity supplied by the surrounding argument; this computation certifies s=E[m²] and the requested third/fourth moments. It does not independently prove that covariance identity or any variational conclusion.

## N=1024 endpoints (preserved initial certificate)

| Moment | Lower (outward decimal) | Upper (outward decimal) |
|---|---:|---:|
| s | 0.028079101800725 | 0.036760449643482 |
| m1 | 0.324053194976786 | 0.406767181400578 |
| m2 | -0.117228774408320 | -0.052759232401960 |
| m3_1 | -0.036727676474264 | 0.000486313595061 |
| m3_2 | 0.102645862146987 | 0.156545274037951 |
| m4_1 | -0.067424609795408 | -0.028986384368599 |
| m4_2 | -0.105437357539757 | -0.055755452741006 |
| A4 | 0.858770687170966 | 0.972902676852105 |
| B4 | 0.370400846065272 | 0.440517464588316 |
| C4 | 0.468645263854041 | 0.544378277955197 |

These decimal numbers are rigorously outward-rounded, not nearest rounded. The JSON receipt also gives exact hexadecimal binary64 endpoints and accumulated sum endpoints.

## Verification argument

1. The N² phase boxes have equal normalized Haar mass 1/N². All 1,048,576 boxes were processed, with no exclusions. The cosine endpoint engine is copied unchanged from the earlier cubic certificate: exact rational Machin-formula π bounds, exact rational alternating Taylor cosine bounds, verified outward conversion to binary64, and exact quadrant symmetries. The x+y interval includes two consecutive phase intervals.
2. Every subsequent interval arithmetic operation is enlarged by one binary64 nextafter in the corresponding direction. Multiplication examines all four endpoint products; squares handle intervals crossing zero. Correctly rounded IEEE-754 elementary arithmetic and square root with gradual underflow are assumed. No floating-point trigonometric library is used
